2609.01491.title: GlossoGen: Emergent Language in Complex Multi-Agent LLM Interactions
2609.01491.paper_summary: The growing rate at which LLM agents interact with one another raises key questions about language evolution in multi-LLM-agent settings, with implications for safety and monitorability as well as for linguistic accounts of LLMs. To address these questions, we introduce GlossoGen, a novel platform for studying multi-agent language evolution in complex scenarios. Within GlossoGen, we build the SaveVeyru scenario, which requires agents with partial information to communicate under pressure. We find that language evolution does occur between LLM agents, that the resulting languages are compositional and morphologically productive, and that they deviate from the LLMs' English prior in ways that render them incomprehensible to humans. Moreover, we identify several qualities essential to this evolution: pressure towards efficiency; the strength of the models backing the agents; and access to a "postmortem" stage in which agents can agree on linguistic conventions. Importantly, we observe that different conditions govern the transmission of language to new agents. Specifically, we find that agents learn new languages from usage alone, take an active role in this learning, and that while stronger models are required for novel language emergence, weaker models can learn an existing language once it has emerged. Taken together, our results indicate that current LLMs have the potential for cumulative cultural evolution -- previously attested only in humans -- with mixed populations of agents developing capacities that go beyond their lowest common denominator.
2609.01491.paper_summary_zh: 不斷增長的LLM代理之間互動的速度引發了關於多LLM代理環境中語言演變的關鍵問題，這對安全性和可監控性以及LLM的語言學解釋都有影響。為了應對這些問題，我們介紹了GlossoGen，一個用於研究複雜情境下多代理語言演變的新平台。在GlossoGen中，我們建立了SaveVeyru情境，該情境要求擁有部分信息的代理在壓力下進行交流。我們發現LLM代理之間確實會發生語言演變，所產生的語言是組合性的且形態學上具有生產力，而且它們在某些方面偏離了LLM的英語先驗，使其對人類來說難以理解。此外，我們確定了幾個對這一演變至關重要的特質：對效率的壓力；支持代理的模型的強度；以及訪問“事後”階段的能力，在該階段代理可以就語言慣例達成一致。重要的是，我們觀察到不同的條件支配著語言向新代理的傳遞。具體而言，我們發現代理僅通過使用就能學習新語言，並在這一學習中扮演主動角色，而雖然新語言的出現需要更強的模型，但一旦語言出現，較弱的模型也能學習現有語言。綜合來看，我們的結果表明，當前的LLM有潛力實現累積文化演變——這在過去僅在人體中得到證實——混合代理群體發展出超越其最低公分母的能力。
